questions.stem: Which statement best defines theology?
options: The study of God and His relationship with creation

questions.stem: Which attribute of God teaches that He is completely independent of His creation?
A believer insists that his personal dreams carry greater authority than Scripture. Which doctrine is being undermined?
Which event introduced sin and death into human history?
General revelation is primarily displayed through:
Which statement best explains the inspiration of Scripture?
options: The Bible contains God’s thoughts mixed with human opinions.
God superintended human authors to communicate His truth accurately.
The Church later declared certain writings inspired.
Scripture became inspired after it was canonized.

questions.stem: Why is historical context important when interpreting Scripture?
options: It limits the application of Scripture.
It helps determine the author’s intended meaning.

questions.stem: Which statement best reflects the biblical doctrine of the Trinity?
options: One God revealed as three distinct Persons sharing one divine essence.
Three gods working together in harmony.
One Person appearing in three different roles.

questions.stem: A Christian refuses to forgive because he believes justice excludes mercy. Which truth corrects this misunderstanding?
options: God’s attributes exist in perfect harmony.

questions.stem: The primary purpose of studying theology is to:
options: Know God rightly and live faithfully.

questions.stem: Which statement best describes doctrine?
options: Organized biblical teaching concerning a subject.

questions.stem: Which of the following is an example of special revelation?
A preacher builds an entire sermon on a single verse without considering the surrounding passage. Which interpretive principle has been neglected?
Which characteristic of Scripture assures believers that God’s Word is completely trustworthy?
God’s promise that the offspring of the woman would defeat the serpent appears first in:
Which divine attribute assures believers that God never changes?
A believer says, “Since God already knows everything, prayer is unnecessary.” Which truth best answers this claim?
options: God ordains both His purposes and the means by which they are accomplished.

questions.stem: Which statement best describes God’s holiness?
options: God is more powerful than creation.
God is morally perfect and completely set apart from sin.

questions.stem: Which statement best summarizes the Bible’s central storyline?
options: God’s work of redemption through Jesus Christ.
The rise of the early Church.

questions.stem: The authority of Scripture means that it:
options: Is the final standard for faith and practice.
Must be interpreted by tradition alone.

questions.stem: Which practice best demonstrates that someone is engaging in theology?
options: Reflecting on what Scripture teaches about God’s character.
Learning ancient languages without studying Scripture.

questions.stem: A Bible teacher consistently points every passage toward God’s redemptive work fulfilled in Christ. Which interpretive approach is he using?
Which attribute assures believers that God possesses complete knowledge of all things?
Why is general revelation insufficient for salvation?
options: It does not reveal God’s saving work in Christ.
It is available only to believers.

questions.stem: Which Person of the Trinity became incarnate?
Which statement best reflects God’s sovereignty?
options: God responds to events He cannot control.
God rules over all creation according to His will.
God shares ultimate authority with humanity.

questions.stem: A student interprets a poetic passage as if it were a legal document. Which principle has been ignored?
Which of the following best describes God’s love?
options: It is perfectly consistent with His holiness.
It changes according to human behavior.

questions.stem: Which statement best explains why Scripture interprets Scripture?
options: Difficult passages should be understood in light of clearer passages.

questions.stem: God’s covenant with Abraham primarily advanced which aspect of redemption?
options: God’s promise to bless all nations through his offspring.

questions.stem: Which statement best explains God’s eternality?
options: God existed before creation but will one day cease.
God exists outside the limitations of time.
God measures time differently from humans.

questions.stem: Which statement correctly describes the relationship between the Father, Son, and Holy Spirit?
options: They are equal in deity and distinct in Person.
The Father alone is fully God.
The Son and Spirit were created.
Each possesses different levels of deity.

questions.stem: A believer bases every doctrine on emotions rather than Scripture. Which danger does this present?
options: Theology becomes rooted in subjective experience.

questions.stem: Which divine attribute assures believers that God is always truthful and dependable?
Why should Christians study theology?
options: To deepen their knowledge of God and strengthen faithful living.

questions.stem: Which biblical event demonstrated God’s judgment while preserving His covenant purposes?
Which doctrine teaches that believers become members of God’s family through Christ?
A Bible reader immediately applies a passage without first asking what it originally meant. Which step has been skipped?
Which characteristic of Scripture makes it the supreme authority for Christian belief?
Which statement best reflects the relationship between God’s justice and mercy?
options: Both are perfectly expressed in God’s character.

questions.stem: Which statement best describes God’s omnipresence?
options: God is present everywhere while remaining distinct from creation.

questions.stem: The ultimate goal of biblical interpretation is to:
options: Discover the author’s intended meaning and faithfully apply it.

questions.stem: Which event most fully accomplished God’s plan of redemption?
options: The life, death, and resurrection of Jesus Christ.

questions.stem: Which statement best describes God’s grace?
Which Person of the Trinity is especially associated with applying God’s redemptive work to believers?
A church member claims that because God is loving, He will never judge sin. Which attribute has been ignored?
Which statement best explains the sufficiency of Scripture?
options: Scripture contains everything necessary for knowing God and living faithfully.
Scripture eliminates the need for teachers.
Scripture replaces the work of the Holy Spirit.

questions.stem: Why is Jesus the climax of divine revelation?
options: He perfectly reveals the Father and fulfills God’s redemptive plan.
He revealed previously unknown attributes of God.

questions.stem: Which statement best reflects the biblical understanding of God’s wisdom?
options: God always accomplishes His perfect purposes in the best possible way.
God’s wisdom is limited to spiritual matters.

questions.stem: Which statement best summarizes the believer’s relationship with God the Father?
options: Believers are adopted into God’s family through Christ and enjoy a personal relationship with Him.
Believers remain servants but never become children.
Believers relate to God only through religious rituals.

questions.stem: A believer says, “God is like us, only much bigger.” Which biblical truth corrects this statement?
options: God is merely a perfected human being.
God is distinct from and infinitely greater than His creation.
God is limited by physical existence.

questions.stem: Which statement best describes God’s self-existence?
options: God depends upon creation for His glory.
God exists because He created Himself.
God exists independently of everything outside Himself.
God derives His life from eternity.

questions.stem: A preacher ignores the Old Testament because he believes it has little value for Christians. Which biblical principle has he overlooked?
options: The unity of God’s redemptive plan.
The independence of the New Testament.
The replacement of Scripture by tradition.

questions.stem: Which statement best describes God’s omnipotence?
options: God can do anything, including contradicting His own nature.
God possesses unlimited power consistent with His character.
God’s power is shared equally with humanity.
God’s power is limited by Satan.

questions.stem: A Christian consistently reads isolated Bible verses without considering the surrounding passage. What is the most likely result?
God’s covenant with Abraham demonstrates that redemption was intended to:
options: Bless all nations through God’s promised Seed.

questions.stem: Which statement best reflects the biblical understanding of God’s justice?
options: God overlooks sin because He is loving.
God always acts according to perfect righteousness.
God’s justice applies only in the Old Testament.

questions.stem: A believer argues that because God is sovereign, human choices have no significance. Which response best reflects biblical teaching?
options: Scripture affirms both God’s sovereignty and human responsibility.

questions.stem: Why should literary genre be considered when interpreting Scripture?
options: Every biblical book follows identical writing patterns.
Different literary forms communicate truth differently.
Poetry should always be interpreted literally.

questions.stem: Which statement best explains the relationship between grace and truth in God’s character?
options: Truth removes the need for grace.
Both are perfectly expressed in God’s dealings with humanity.

questions.stem: Which event demonstrates God’s faithfulness despite human failure?
options: God’s continued unfolding of His covenant promises after humanity sinned.

questions.stem: Which doctrine teaches that God has eternally existed as Father, Son, and Holy Spirit?
Which statement best explains why Jesus is central to Scripture?
options: He appears in every verse by name.
The entire biblical narrative finds its fulfillment in Him.
The Old Testament is unrelated to Him.

questions.stem: A church member claims that everyone interprets Scripture correctly regardless of context. Which principle corrects this assumption?
options: Meaning is determined by the original author’s intent.

questions.stem: Which characteristic distinguishes God from every created being?
Why is Scripture described as sufficient?
options: It provides everything necessary for faith and godly living.
It removes the need for teachers.

questions.stem: A believer says that God learned from history. Which divine attribute refutes this claim?
Which statement best summarizes the purpose of divine revelation?
options: To make God known and reveal His redemptive purposes.

questions.stem: Which statement best reflects biblical worship?
options: Worship is a life of reverence and obedience flowing from knowing God.
Worship belongs only in church gatherings.

questions.stem: Which doctrine explains why believers can confidently call God “Father”?
A teacher presents God’s love without mentioning His holiness. What imbalance has occurred?
options: God’s character has been separated into competing attributes.

questions.stem: Which event marked God’s judgment on humanity while preserving His covenant purposes through one family?
Which statement best describes the relationship between Scripture and tradition?
options: Tradition has equal authority with Scripture.
Scripture is the final authority by which all traditions are evaluated.
Scripture depends upon tradition for authority.

questions.stem: Which of the following best demonstrates theological maturity?
options: Growing in accurate knowledge of God that transforms daily living.

questions.stem: Which statement best explains why the Bible forms one unified story?
options: Every book has the same human author.
God’s redemptive purpose unites all of Scripture.
Every book was written at the same time.
The New Testament replaces the Old Testament.

questions.stem: A Christian believes God is present only inside church buildings. Which attribute corrects this misunderstanding?
Which statement best reflects the doctrine of creation?
options: God created everything and sustains it by His power.

questions.stem: Why should Christians interpret individual passages within the larger story of Scripture?
options: Because every passage contributes to God’s unified redemptive plan.

questions.stem: Which statement best reflects biblical faith?
options: Faith responds in trust to God’s revealed truth.

questions.stem: Which statement best explains God’s mercy?
options: God compassionately withholds the judgment sinners deserve.

questions.stem: A person says the Father is fully God, but the Son is less than God. Which doctrine is being denied?
options: The full deity of the Son within the Trinity.

questions.stem: Which statement best reflects the relationship between theology and Christian living?
options: Theology is unrelated to practical life.

questions.stem: Which event demonstrates God’s promise to reverse the curse introduced by sin?
Why should believers read Scripture prayerfully?
options: The Holy Spirit illuminates believers to understand and apply God’s Word.
Prayer removes the need for context.

questions.stem: Which statement best reflects God’s wisdom?
options: God chooses good options after careful consideration.
God perfectly knows and accomplishes His purposes.

questions.stem: Which statement best explains the believer’s confidence in God’s promises?
Which statement best explains why redemption is necessary?
A student immediately asks, “How does this apply to me?” before determining what the text means. Which principle has been overlooked?
Which statement best describes the relationship between God and truth?
options: God is the ultimate standard of truth.

questions.stem: Which biblical truth provides the strongest basis for Christian identity?
options: Adoption into God’s family through Christ.

questions.stem: Which statement best summarizes God’s purpose in revealing Himself?
options: To invite people into a relationship with Him through His redemptive work.

questions.stem: Which statement best reflects biblical humility in theology?
options: Submitting one’s beliefs to the authority of Scripture.

questions.stem: Which attribute assures believers that God is always present with them?
A Christian concludes that because God disciplines His children, He no longer loves them. Which doctrine best corrects this misunderstanding?
options: Divine love and fatherly discipline work together for believers’ good.
Discipline belongs only under the Old Covenant.

questions.stem: Which statement best explains why Christ is called the fulfillment of Scripture?
options: He completed God’s redemptive promises and purposes revealed throughout Scripture.

questions.stem: Which statement best describes God’s holiness?
options: God is simply greater than humanity.
God is morally perfect and completely set apart from all sin.

questions.stem: Why is careful theological study important for the Church?
options: It protects believers from error and strengthens faithful discipleship.
It guarantees agreement on every issue.
It eliminates the need for preaching.

questions.stem: Which statement best summarizes the biblical understanding of God’s Fatherhood?
options: God is Father only because He created humanity.
Through Christ, believers enjoy a personal relationship with God as their Father.
God relates only to Israel as Father.
God is Father only in the New Testament.

questions.stem: A believer says that one attribute of God is more important than all the others. Which theological principle best addresses this claim?
options: God’s attributes exist in perfect unity and harmony.

questions.stem: Which statement best summarizes the goal of this course?
options: To know God more accurately through His self-revelation and faithfully live in light of His truth.
